source:
Inez: Expand the homework text-message pilot. The spring report says 62 percent of participating students submitted homework on time, compared with 48 percent in the matched class that did not get texts.
Oren: The same report says only 18 of 70 eligible students used it at least twice. A result from that small opt-in group is not enough to make it districtwide.
Inez: The on-time gap is the best evidence we have.
Oren: The participation number is the warning label on that evidence.

extraction.mainQuestion: Is the homework text-message pilot evidence strong enough to expand districtwide?

positions.label: Expand the pilot
positions.thesis: The district should expand the homework text-message pilot because the report shows higher on-time submission among participants.
positions.steelman: The matched-class comparison suggests the text-message pilot may be improving homework submission.

positions.label: Do not expand yet
positions.thesis: The district should not expand the pilot because the evidence comes from a small opt-in group.
positions.steelman: Low participation makes the result too fragile to justify a districtwide rollout.

groundingQuotes.quote: A result from that small opt-in group is not enough to make it districtwide.

claims.statement: Participating students had a 62 percent on-time submission rate compared with 48 percent in a matched class.

resolution.condition: Inspect the spring report's matched-class comparison and methodology.

groundingQuotes.quote: 62 percent of participating students submitted homework on time, compared with 48 percent in the matched class

claims.statement: Only 18 of 70 eligible students used the text-message pilot at least twice.

resolution.condition: Inspect the report's participation denominator and opt-in process.

groundingQuotes.quote: only 18 of 70 eligible students used it at least twice.

disagreementCandidates.question: Does the report's on-time submission gap outweigh the low participation concern?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Inez cites the outcome gap; Oren cites the low participation denominator.

participantStances.stance: The report is strong enough to expand.
The report is too weak because participation was low.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Evaluate the report's design, denominator, and effect estimate.

caveats: The numbers are cited by speakers in the source and are not independently verified here.
